We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM is seeking a growth-oriented Management Consulting Director to join our Technology Performance practice. This leader will play a critical role in driving the continued growth of the practice by expanding strategic client relationships, developing new market opportunities, and leading complex technology transformation engagements.

This Director will combine strong business development capabilities with deep expertise in Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy, IT Architecture, and complex transformation program leadership. The role requires a leader who can originate opportunities, shape solutions, build trusted executive relationships, oversee complex engagements, and develop high-performing consulting teams.

This individual will also help shape the continued evolution of the Technology Performance practice by developing talent, strengthening capabilities, and bringing differentiated solutions to market.

Responsibilities

Practice Growth & Market Leadership

Drive growth of the Technology Performance practice through business development, account expansion, relationship building, and new client acquisition.
Build and manage a strong pipeline of technology consulting and transformation opportunities.
Develop trusted relationships with senior executives, including CIOs, CTOs, CFOs, COOs, and other business and technology leaders.
Lead strategic pursuits from opportunity identification and solution development through proposal creation, executive presentations, and contract award.
Identify opportunities to expand existing client relationships by connecting business priorities with RSM’s broader technology and consulting capabilities.
Develop and execute go-to-market strategies around key Technology Performance offerings and emerging client needs.
Contribute to the practice’s market presence through thought leadership, industry events, executive presentations, and development of differentiated offerings.

Client & Engagement Leadership

Serve as a senior trusted advisor to executives navigating complex technology strategies, investments, and transformation programs.
Lead engagements spanning Technology Strategy, ERP Strategy and Selection, IT Architecture, enterprise application modernization, digital transformation, and technology operating model design.
Advise clients on aligning technology investments and roadmaps with business strategy, growth objectives, operational needs, and financial priorities.
Lead and oversee complex, multi-workstream transformation programs involving business stakeholders, technology teams, vendors, and third-party partners.
Lead executive workshops, technology assessments, and strategy sessions and translate findings into actionable transformation roadmaps.
Provide executive oversight across engagements, ensuring high-quality delivery, strong client relationships, financial performance, appropriate risk management, and successful business outcomes.

Advise clients on ERP strategy, modernization, selection, implementation planning, and optimization, including the broader business and operating model implications of ERP transformation.
Assess existing IT and enterprise architecture and develop future-state architectures that support scalability, integration, modernization, and business objectives.
Provide leadership across complex technology environments involving ERP, cloud, data and analytics, AI, automation, enterprise applications, infrastructure, and integration architecture.

jobs.description:
We’re building a relationship-oriented bank for the modern world. We need talented, passionate professionals who are dedicated to doing what’s right for our clients.

At CIBC, we embrace your strengths and your ambitions, so you are empowered at work. Our team members have what they need to make a meaningful impact and are truly valued for who they are and what they contribute.

To learn more about CIBC, please visit CIBC.com

What You'll Be Doing

Collections is a dynamic, high-impact team focused on delivering effective client treatment strategies while balancing client experience, operational efficiency, and regulatory requirements. As Director, Collections Channel Management, you will own the end-to-end management and optimization of Collections contact channels, including voice and dialer, short message service (SMS), email, digital, self-service, and emerging channels. You will lead channel performance, controls, and continuous improvement so that channels work together to deliver effective client treatments, operational efficiency, and strong Collections outcomes. Over the next two years, you will also be the business lead for the new Dialer, from requirements and design through launch, stabilization, and optimization. Working closely with partners across Technology, Operations, Risk, Analytics, Digital, and vendors, you'll help build scalable channel capabilities that strengthen Collections performance today and support long-term omnichannel evolution.

At CIBC we enable the work environment most optimal for you to thrive in your role. You'll have the flexibility to manage your work activities within a hybrid work arrangement where you'll spend 1-3 days per week on-site, while other days will be remote.

How You'll Succeed

Channel strategy and optimization - Own the operating model for Collections channels and define how channels are used, including treatment paths, prioritization, sequencing, and intraday management. Continuously refine channel mix and execution using performance insights to improve effectiveness, efficiency, and client experience.
Dialer transformation leadership - Act as the business lead for the Dialer transformation, from requirements and design through implementation, migration, launch, and optimization. Define business requirements, set acceptance criteria, and ensure testing, controls, reporting, and readiness activities support a successful rollout.
Omnichannel treatment execution - Partner with Credit Risk, Operations, Analytics, Digital, and Technology to deliver integrated contact strategies that align to client needs, risk, and operational capacity. Lead test-and-learn initiatives that improve engagement, digital adoption, treatment effectiveness, and client outcomes.
Governance, risk, and controls - Establish clear decision rights and governance for channel and contact strategy decisions across key stakeholder groups. Ensure channel activity complies with policies, contact rules, consent and preference requirements, calling windows, and regulatory expectations.
Performance management and continuous improvement - Monitor channel metrics such as right-party contact, promise-to-pay, cure, and cost-to-collect, and connect performance results to broader Collections and operational outcomes. Use insights and reporting to identify opportunities, manage risks, and drive continuous improvement.
Partnership and change leadership - Bring together partners across Business, Technology, Risk, Operations, Digital, Analytics, and vendor teams to deliver common outcomes. Communicate clearly with senior leaders, manage escalations, and support change adoption throughout transformation delivery.

Who You Are

You can demonstrate experience in Collections, channel management, contact-centre transformation, credit operations, digital servicing, and operating in a highly regulated environment. It’s an asset if you have experience within a financial institution and across large-scale client contact ecosystems.
You give meaning to data. You enjoy investigating complex problems and making sense of information. You communicate detailed information in a meaningful way.
Your influence makes a difference. You know that relationships and networks are essential to success. You inspire outcomes by sharing your expertise.
You act like an owner. You thrive when you're empowered to take initiative, go above and beyond, and deliver results.
You are a caring and accountable leader. You have experience developing and implementing strategic team goals. You have experience coaching employees and inspiring successful team performance.
You live your values. You bring high standards, genuine care to your relationships, and want to grow with an employer that shares your values and brings out your best.

What CIBC Offers

At CIBC, your goals are a priority. We start with your strengths and ambitions as an employee and strive to create opportunities to tap into your potential. We aspire to give you a career, rather than just a paycheck.

We work to recognize you in meaningful, personalized ways including a competitive salary, incentive pay, banking benefits, a benefits program*, defined benefit pension plan*, an employee share purchase plan, a vacation offering, wellbeing support, and MomentMakers, our social, points-based recognition program.
Our spaces and technological toolkit will make it simple to bring together great minds to create innovative solutions that make a difference for our clients.

jobs.description:
Why Valtech? We’re the experience innovation company - a trusted partner to the world’s most recognized brands. To our people we offer growth opportunities, a values-driven culture, international careers and the chance to shape the future of experience.

The opportunity

At Valtech, you’ll find an environment designed for continuous learning, meaningful impact, and professional growth. Whether you're pioneering new digital solutions, challenging conventional thinking or building the next generation of customer experiences, your work will help transform industries.

We Are Proud Of

The work we do and the innovation we drive
Our values of share, care and dare
A workplace culture that fosters creativity, diversity and autonomy
Our borderless, global framework, which enables seamless collaboration

The role

Please note, we are only accepting applicants from the provinces of Ontario and Québec for this role.
For Québec-based candidates, fluency in English is necessary because the position entails collaboration with teams based in the rest of Americas and occasionally in Europe.

As Practice Director, Shopify Commerce, you will own the technical vision, delivery excellence, and business development strategy for our enterprise Shopify Plus practice. You will lead a global team of architects, engineers, and solution consultants—shaping how we design, build, and scale mission-critical commerce platforms for our largest clients. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise commerce architecture, active sales engagement, and talent leadership. You will be expected to command deep, hands-on knowledge of the Shopify Plus ecosystem and the broader technology stack that surrounds it—including ERP integrations, enterprise search, customer data platforms, and headless commerce patterns—and translate that expertise into winning proposals, trusted client partnerships, and a world-class team.

Why Join Us?

Lead a practice at the forefront of enterprise Shopify Plus—working with some of the world’s most ambitious commerce brands.
Collaborate with global experts across strategy, design, engineering, and commerce operations to deliver end-to-end transformation.
Shape how our firm thinks about and delivers Shopify—building playbooks, growing a team, and influencing the direction of a high-growth practice.

Role Responsibilities

Shopify Plus Architecture & Technology Strategy

Define and own the architectural patterns and best practices for enterprise Shopify Plus deployments, including headless/composable commerce, Shopify Functions, Markets Pro, and B2B capabilities.
Lead the design of end-to-end commerce ecosystems spanning Shopify Plus and adjacent enterprise systems—ERP (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia, Kenshoo), CDP/CRM (Salesforce, Segment, mParticle), PIM, OMS, and payment gateways.
Evaluate and stay ahead of emerging Shopify platform capabilities (e.g., Shopify Audiences, Checkout Extensibility, Editions releases) and translate them into client-ready solutions and internal playbooks.
Serve as the practice’s ultimate authority on technical feasibility, scalability, and integration strategy for Shopify Plus engagements.

Delivery Leadership

Oversee technical delivery across global, cross-functional teams delivering enterprise Shopify Plus solutions, ensuring quality, performance, and client satisfaction at scale.
Establish governance frameworks, risk mitigation strategies, and delivery KPIs tailored to the pace and complexity of commerce platform engagements. -
Act as a technical escalation point and actively unblock delivery teams, modeling the kind of senior leadership and decisiveness the practice requires.
Build, retain, and develop a high-performing team of Shopify architects, engineers, and solution leads—setting clear expectations, creating growth paths, and fostering a culture of technical excellence.

Sales Engagement & Client Partnership

Own the technical narrative in the sales process: participate actively in discovery, solutioning, estimation, architecture design, and proposal development for Shopify Plus pursuits.
Partner closely with business development and account teams to identify upsell and cross-sell opportunities within existing Shopify Plus engagements.
Serve as a credible, senior technical voice in client-facing conversations—building trust, managing expectations, and positioning our practice as a strategic partner, not just a vendor.
Maintain and deepen relationships with Shopify’s partner and alliance teams, ensuring we are positioned for early access to new programs, beta capabilities, and co-sell opportunities.

Practice Development & Talent Growth

Mentor and coach Shopify architects, technical leads, and engineers across regions—actively investing in their growth and career trajectories.
Drive Shopify-specific certification and enablement programs (e.g., Shopify Partner certifications, Shopify Developer certifications) and build learning paths that keep the team at the forefront of platform innovation.
Contribute to internal knowledge sharing, solution playbooks, case studies, and reusable architecture assets that accelerate delivery and sales across the practice.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Utilization Optimization: Maintain or improve team utilization rates across all Shopify Plus engagements, targeting 70%+ blended team utilization.
Certification Growth: Drive 100% of the practice team to hold at least one Shopify Partner or Developer certification within 12 months.
Solution Quality: Ensure architectural integrity, scalability, and maintainability across all delivered Shopify Plus solutions—measured by client satisfaction scores and post-launch performance benchmarks.
Sales Pipeline Contribution: Actively participate in pursuits contributing to at least $8M in unweighted Shopify Commerce pipeline annually, with a target of closing $3M+ in new logos or significant expansions.
Individual Billability: Maintain a minimum of 50% individual billable utilization, balanced against the practice-building and sales activities inherent to this role.
Team Retention & Growth: Achieve 85%+ retention within the practice and maintain a pipeline of at least two internal candidates ready for promotion annually.

Must Have Qualifications

To be considered for this role, you must meet the following essential qualifications:

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology leadership within a consulting, systems integration, or agency environment—with at least 3–4 years specifically in Shopify Plus or a comparable enterprise commerce platform.
Deep, hands-on expertise in the Shopify Plus platform: Shopify Functions, Checkout Extensibility, Markets Pro, B2B, headless/composable commerce architectures, and the Shopify app ecosystem.
Strong command of the enterprise commerce technology stack surrounding Shopify Plus—including ERP integrations (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite), enterprise search (Elasticsearch, Algolia), CDPs (Segment, mParticle, Salesforce Data Cloud), PIM, OMS, and payment platforms.
Proven track record of participating in or leading sales pursuits, proposals, and client-facing solutioning conversations—comfortable owning a technical narrative in a competitive deal.
Experience building, leading, and growing distributed technical teams—hiring, mentoring, retaining senior talent, and creating cultures of technical excellence.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills; able to operate fluently across executive, technical, and commercial audiences.

Preferred Certifications

Shopify Partner Certification, Shopify Developer Certification, or Shopify Plus Certification (required or expected within 6 months of hire).
AWS/Azure/GCP Solutions Architect, TOGAF, SAFe, PMP, or equivalent—demonstrating both platform-level and enterprise architecture credentials.

Commitment to reaching all kinds of people

We design experiences that work for all kinds of people - and that starts with our own teams. At Valtech, we’re intentional about building an inclusive culture where everyone feels supported to grow, thrive and achieve their goals. No matter your background, you belong here. Explore our Diversity & Inclusion site to see how we’re creating a more equitable Valtech for all.

About The Role

We are seeking an experienced and collaborative leader to join H&R Block Canada as Interim Director, Products & Services for a 12-month term. The Interim Director will provide leadership and continuity for the Associate Products & Services portfolio, working with an established team of Product Management professionals to maintain focus, coordination, and delivery against established priorities.

This role is well suited to a leader who can quickly build an understanding of the portfolio, work effectively through subject-matter experts, and provide clear direction and oversight. The Interim Director will support the team in advancing product and service priorities while engaging cross-functional partners and senior leaders as appropriate. This position is based in Calgary and offers a hybrid work schedule, with 3 days per week in-office.

Reporting Structure and Team

Reporting to the Vice President, Products & Services, the Interim Director provides leadership to a team of Product Management professionals across senior product management, product management, associate product management, and digital product management roles. The Interim Director will work closely with these experienced team members, provide direction and support, remove barriers, and escalate matters as appropriate.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Leadership and Team Support

Provide day-to-day leadership and continuity for the team throughout the 12-month term.
Build an understanding of current priorities, products, stakeholders, and ways of working through a structured transition and ongoing partnership with the team.
Set clear expectations, support decision-making, hold regular check-ins, and help team members remain aligned on priorities and commitments.
Coach and support direct reports while drawing on their expertise in product management, UX, technology, and other relevant functional areas.
Create an environment where issues are raised early and work with the team and senior leaders to resolve issues and identify practical solutions.

Oversight of Products and Services

Oversee progress against established product and service plans, including priorities related to small business, specialty tax, Block Pro, Core/CIS, and digital products.
Work with Product Managers to review roadmaps, milestones, risks, dependencies, and launch readiness while maintaining appropriate accountability for delivery.
Support the team in maintaining oversight of product performance, budgets, client impacts, and field operational considerations.
Help ensure recommendations and decisions are supported by available data, client feedback, and the expertise of responsible team members.
Maintain awareness of financial services work within the portfolio and engage subject-matter experts and senior leaders when specialized guidance or approvals are required.

Cross-Functional Coordination

Coordinate with internal partners to maintain momentum on agreed priorities and clarify roles, timelines, and decision points.
Facilitate collaboration among Product Management, UX Design & Content Strategy, technology, operations, delivery services and PMG, marketing, finance, and other stakeholders as required.
Provide clear updates to senior leadership on progress, risks, resource needs, and decisions requiring additional support.
Maintain existing third-party and vendor relationships in partnership with the appropriate internal owners, escalating material issues as required.
Support existing Tax Pro and franchisee focus groups and manage feedback and escalations relating to Associate products.

jobs.description:
“Join us in
building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”

About Us

At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

The Opportunity

The Director, Sales Operations
is responsible for owning, standardizing, and continuously improving the commercial operating system across the organization. This is a corporate role working in collaboration with all sales regions in the Atlantic Packaging network (Ontario, Quebec, USA).

This role does not own sales targets nor manage sales teams directly. Instead, it enables Sales Leadership and P&L owners to execute consistently by providing clear processes, disciplined governance, and effective tools.

The role addresses recurring structural issues in sales execution (contracts, risk exposure, forecast visibility, onboarding effectiveness, and CRM adoption) and brings process excellence to an area historically driven by individual experience rather than system discipline. Sales Operations builds the system so Sales / Marketing / Legal / Finance / CX work together efficiently.

The corporate Customer Experience function will report into the Director, Sales Operations, which expect will increase the probability that customer feedback results in retention, growth, and operational improvement.

Success Factors in the Role

Success in this role will be judged on system outcomes, not activity.

Sales execution becomes repeatable
Fewer deal-specific workarounds; consistent deal flow through the same stages and approvals.

Sales leaders use the tools willingly
Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.

Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)
P&L owners can see contract duration mix, terms exposure, and liability accumulation before approving deals.

Fewer “surprises”
Fewer last-minute escalations due to undocumented terms, unclear approvals, or cross‑region inconsistencies.

Improved funnel credibility
Forecast discussions are grounded in a shared, disciplined view of the pipeline.

CX feedback loop is integrated into the sales process which will result in better CX scores across the businesses

What You’ll Do

This role sets standards and runs governance. Sales Leadership owns execution. Finance/Credit/Legal co-own approval rules and risk thresholds.

Sales Operating Model & Governance
Own and maintain the front-end sales operating model, including:
Contract approval workflows and limits of authority (with Legal).
Clear rules when customers operate across regions.

Partner with Legal, Finance, and Credit to make risk explicit and decision-ready.
Ensure P&L leaders have visibility before commitments are made, not after.
Salesforce Ownership
Act as business owner of Salesforce (process design, usage standards, reporting logic).
Drive adoption by defining how and why Salesforce is used:
Funnel structure aligned with business needs (product mix, seasonality, capacity).
Standard dashboards for P&L owners and Sales Leadership.

Reduce “system noise” so the tool supports decisions, not administration.
Funnel Management & Sales Planning
Define and enforce consistent funnel management practices.
Provide forward-looking visibility on revenue concentration by:
Factory
Asset type
Industry
Salesperson
Other cuts as needed

Enable proactive capacity and production discussions (vs. reactive firefighting).
Drive development of sales plans that can be handed off for execution.
Enable consolidation of this data for the Group.
Contract, Terms & Risk Tracking
Implement standardized reporting on:
Contract tenure mix (no contract, quarterly, annual, etc.).
Payment terms exposure.
Aggregate liability commitments.

Make commercial risk measured, visible, and discussable (not implicit or anecdotal).
Sales Training / Motivation / Sales incentive management
Design and institutionalize a formal sales onboarding and training framework.
Develop role-specific training (e.g., Salesforce usage, contract basics).
Build a repeatable cadence for sales meetings to drive consistent themes and execution.
Administer the sales incentive program, including consistent publishing of performance vs. targets.
Manage corporate CX program

What You Bring

Strong background in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Revenue Enablement.
Must be fluent in both French/English
Comfortable influencing senior sales leaders without hierarchical authority.
Process-oriented, systems thinker with a strong business bias.
Credible with Finance, Sales, and Operations alike.
Required: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.
7+ years of experience in progressive experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Business Analytics
Expert in Salesforce, specifically in design, governance and adoption.

What We Offer

Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)
Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events
A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition
Opportunities for advancement and internal movement
Education assistance for continuous skill development
Academic scholarships for employees’ children
Safety equipment and PPE support program
Retirement savings and wellness initiatives
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Inclusion and Accessibility

Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please Note

Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

Sommaire du rôle

Le/La Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives est responsable de définir, standardiser et améliorer en continu le système d’exploitation commercial de l’organisation. Il s’agit d’un rôle corporatif qui travaille en collaboration avec toutes les régions de ventes du réseau Atlantic Packaging, incluant l’Ontario, le Québec et les États-Unis.

Ce rôle n’est pas propriétaire des objectifs de ventes et ne gère pas directement les équipes de ventes. Son rôle est plutôt de permettre aux leaders des ventes et aux responsables P&L d’exécuter de façon constante, en mettant en place des processus clairs, une gouvernance disciplinée et des outils efficaces.

Le rôle adresse des enjeux structurels récurrents dans l’exécution commerciale, notamment les contrats, l’exposition aux risques, la visibilité sur le funnel, l’efficacité de l’intégration des nouveaux employés et l’adoption de Salesforce. Il amène de la rigueur de processus dans une fonction qui a historiquement reposé davantage sur l’expérience individuelle que sur une discipline institutionnelle. Les opérations commerciales corporatives bâtissent le système pour permettre aux Ventes / Marketing / Légal / Finances / CX de travailler ensemble efficacement.

La fonction corporative d’expérience client relèvera du/de la Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives, ce qui est un arrimage naturel puisque la Voix du client, l’adoption de Salesforce, la discipline du funnel, la boucle fermée et les cadences commerciales doivent être connectées au même système de gestion pour transformer les commentaires clients en actions concrètes, soutenir la rétention, favoriser la croissance et améliorer l’exécution opérationnelle.

Facteurs de succès dans le rôle

Le succès dans ce rôle sera évalué sur les résultats du système, et non sur le niveau d’activité.

L’exécution des ventes devient reproductible
Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

Les leaders des ventes utilisent les outils parce qu’ils les aident à gérer le business
Salesforce est utilisé parce qu’il facilite la gestion commerciale, et non seulement parce qu’il est obligatoire.

Les risques commerciaux sont visibles avant les décisions
Les responsables P&L peuvent voir la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité avant d’approuver les ententes.

Moins de surprises
Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

Crédibilité accrue du funnel
Les discussions de prévisions sont basées sur une vision partagée et disciplinée du pipeline.

La boucle de rétroaction CX est intégrée au processus de ventes afin d’améliorer les scores CX dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires.

Portée et responsabilités clés

Ce rôle établit les standards et anime la gouvernance. Les leaders des ventes demeurent propriétaires de l’exécution. Les finances, le crédit et le légal codéfinissent les règles d’approbation et les seuils de risque.

Modèle opérationnel des ventes et gouvernance
Définir et maintenir le modèle opérationnel commercial de première ligne, incluant les flux d’approbation des contrats, les limites d’autorité et les règles applicables aux clients opérant dans plusieurs régions.
Travailler avec le juridique, les finances et le crédit afin de rendre le risque explicite et prêt à être décidé.
S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.
Ownership Salesforce
Agir comme propriétaire d’affaires de Salesforce pour le design des processus, les standards d’utilisation et la logique de reporting.
Favoriser l’adoption en définissant clairement comment et pourquoi Salesforce est utilisé.
Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.
Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.
Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.
Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes
Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.
Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.
Permettre des discussions proactives sur la capacité et la production, plutôt que de fonctionner en mode réaction ou escalade.
Contribuer au développement de plans de ventes clairs, prêts à être transférés en exécution.
Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.
Contrats, termes et suivi des risques
Mettre en place un reporting standardisé sur la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité.
Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.
Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes
Concevoir et institutionnaliser un cadre formel d’intégration et de formation pour les équipes de ventes.
Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.
Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.
Administrer le programme d’incitatifs de ventes, incluant la publication constante de la performance par rapport aux objectifs.

new_jobs.description:
“Join us in
building Careers and shaping Experiences Beyond the Box”

About Us

At Atlantic Packaging, every box tells a story and yours begins here. As a proudly Canadian-owned company with over 80 years of excellence in the corrugated packaging industry with operations within North America (Ontario, Quebec and United States), we’re committed to sustainability, customer excellence and community impact. Since 1945, we’ve supported local jobs and built a legacy of trust with our clients and team members. At Atlantic, your ideas matter, your growth is supported and your work makes a real impact.

The Opportunity

The Director, Sales Operations
is responsible for owning, standardizing, and continuously improving the commercial operating system across the organization. This is a corporate role working in collaboration with all sales regions in the Atlantic Packaging network (Ontario, Quebec, USA).

This role does not own sales targets nor manage sales teams directly. Instead, it enables Sales Leadership and P&L owners to execute consistently by providing clear processes, disciplined governance, and effective tools.

The role addresses recurring structural issues in sales execution (contracts, risk exposure, forecast visibility, onboarding effectiveness, and CRM adoption) and brings process excellence to an area historically driven by individual experience rather than system discipline. Sales Operations builds the system so Sales / Marketing / Legal / Finance / CX work together efficiently.

The corporate Customer Experience function will report into the Director, Sales Operations, which expect will increase the probability that customer feedback results in retention, growth, and operational improvement.

Success Factors in the Role

Success in this role will be judged on system outcomes, not activity.

Sales execution becomes repeatable
Fewer deal-specific workarounds; consistent deal flow through the same stages and approvals.

Sales leaders use the tools willingly
Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.

Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)
P&L owners can see contract duration mix, terms exposure, and liability accumulation before approving deals.

Fewer “surprises”
Fewer last-minute escalations due to undocumented terms, unclear approvals, or cross‑region inconsistencies.

Improved funnel credibility
Forecast discussions are grounded in a shared, disciplined view of the pipeline.

CX feedback loop is integrated into the sales process which will result in better CX scores across the businesses

What You’ll Do

This role sets standards and runs governance. Sales Leadership owns execution. Finance/Credit/Legal co-own approval rules and risk thresholds.

Sales Operating Model & Governance
Own and maintain the front-end sales operating model, including:
Contract approval workflows and limits of authority (with Legal).
Clear rules when customers operate across regions.

Partner with Legal, Finance, and Credit to make risk explicit and decision-ready.
Ensure P&L leaders have visibility before commitments are made, not after.
Salesforce Ownership
Act as business owner of Salesforce (process design, usage standards, reporting logic).
Drive adoption by defining how and why Salesforce is used:
Funnel structure aligned with business needs (product mix, seasonality, capacity).
Standard dashboards for P&L owners and Sales Leadership.

Reduce “system noise” so the tool supports decisions, not administration.
Funnel Management & Sales Planning
Define and enforce consistent funnel management practices.
Provide forward-looking visibility on revenue concentration by:
Factory
Asset type
Industry
Salesperson
Other cuts as needed

Enable proactive capacity and production discussions (vs. reactive firefighting).
Drive development of sales plans that can be handed off for execution.
Enable consolidation of this data for the Group.
Contract, Terms & Risk Tracking
Implement standardized reporting on:
Contract tenure mix (no contract, quarterly, annual, etc.).
Payment terms exposure.
Aggregate liability commitments.

Make commercial risk measured, visible, and discussable (not implicit or anecdotal).
Sales Training / Motivation / Sales incentive management
Design and institutionalize a formal sales onboarding and training framework.
Develop role-specific training (e.g., Salesforce usage, contract basics).
Build a repeatable cadence for sales meetings to drive consistent themes and execution.
Administer the sales incentive program, including consistent publishing of performance vs. targets.
Manage corporate CX program

What You Bring

Strong background in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Revenue Enablement.
Must be fluent in both French/English
Comfortable influencing senior sales leaders without hierarchical authority.
Process-oriented, systems thinker with a strong business bias.
Credible with Finance, Sales, and Operations alike.
Required: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Commerce, Finance, Operations, or a related field required.
7+ years of experience in progressive experience in Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Commercial Excellence, or Business Analytics
Expert in Salesforce, specifically in design, governance and adoption.

What We Offer

Comprehensive health, dental and vision coverage (dependents included)
Teamwork-focused culture with sustainability initiatives and social events
A culture of appreciation through a point-based recognition
Opportunities for advancement and internal movement
Education assistance for continuous skill development
Academic scholarships for employees’ children
Safety equipment and PPE support program
Retirement savings and wellness initiatives
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Inclusion and Accessibility

Atlantic Packaging is committed to fostering an inclusive, accessible and respectful environment for all candidates. If you require accommodation during the hiring process, please contact our Talent Acquisition team—we’re here to support you.

We sincerely thank all applicants for their interest in joining Atlantic Packaging. While we appreciate the time and effort invested, only those selected for an interview will be contacted.

Please Note

Candidates who are 18 years or older are required to complete a criminal and background check. Details will be provided through the application process.

Sommaire du rôle

Le/La Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives est responsable de définir, standardiser et améliorer en continu le système d’exploitation commercial de l’organisation. Il s’agit d’un rôle corporatif qui travaille en collaboration avec toutes les régions de ventes du réseau Atlantic Packaging, incluant l’Ontario, le Québec et les États-Unis.

Ce rôle n’est pas propriétaire des objectifs de ventes et ne gère pas directement les équipes de ventes. Son rôle est plutôt de permettre aux leaders des ventes et aux responsables P&L d’exécuter de façon constante, en mettant en place des processus clairs, une gouvernance disciplinée et des outils efficaces.

Le rôle adresse des enjeux structurels récurrents dans l’exécution commerciale, notamment les contrats, l’exposition aux risques, la visibilité sur le funnel, l’efficacité de l’intégration des nouveaux employés et l’adoption de Salesforce. Il amène de la rigueur de processus dans une fonction qui a historiquement reposé davantage sur l’expérience individuelle que sur une discipline institutionnelle. Les opérations commerciales corporatives bâtissent le système pour permettre aux Ventes / Marketing / Légal / Finances / CX de travailler ensemble efficacement.

La fonction corporative d’expérience client relèvera du/de la Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives, ce qui est un arrimage naturel puisque la Voix du client, l’adoption de Salesforce, la discipline du funnel, la boucle fermée et les cadences commerciales doivent être connectées au même système de gestion pour transformer les commentaires clients en actions concrètes, soutenir la rétention, favoriser la croissance et améliorer l’exécution opérationnelle.

Facteurs de succès dans le rôle

Le succès dans ce rôle sera évalué sur les résultats du système, et non sur le niveau d’activité.

L’exécution des ventes devient reproductible
Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

Les leaders des ventes utilisent les outils parce qu’ils les aident à gérer le business
Salesforce est utilisé parce qu’il facilite la gestion commerciale, et non seulement parce qu’il est obligatoire.

Les risques commerciaux sont visibles avant les décisions
Les responsables P&L peuvent voir la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité avant d’approuver les ententes.

Moins de surprises
Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

Crédibilité accrue du funnel
Les discussions de prévisions sont basées sur une vision partagée et disciplinée du pipeline.

La boucle de rétroaction CX est intégrée au processus de ventes afin d’améliorer les scores CX dans l’ensemble des unités d’affaires.

Portée et responsabilités clés

Ce rôle établit les standards et anime la gouvernance. Les leaders des ventes demeurent propriétaires de l’exécution. Les finances, le crédit et le légal codéfinissent les règles d’approbation et les seuils de risque.

Modèle opérationnel des ventes et gouvernance
Définir et maintenir le modèle opérationnel commercial de première ligne, incluant les flux d’approbation des contrats, les limites d’autorité et les règles applicables aux clients opérant dans plusieurs régions.
Travailler avec le juridique, les finances et le crédit afin de rendre le risque explicite et prêt à être décidé.
S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.
Ownership Salesforce
Agir comme propriétaire d’affaires de Salesforce pour le design des processus, les standards d’utilisation et la logique de reporting.
Favoriser l’adoption en définissant clairement comment et pourquoi Salesforce est utilisé.
Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.
Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.
Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.
Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes
Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.
Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.
Permettre des discussions proactives sur la capacité et la production, plutôt que de fonctionner en mode réaction ou escalade.
Contribuer au développement de plans de ventes clairs, prêts à être transférés en exécution.
Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.
Contrats, termes et suivi des risques
Mettre en place un reporting standardisé sur la durée des contrats, l’exposition aux termes de paiement et les engagements de responsabilité.
Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.
Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes
Concevoir et institutionnaliser un cadre formel d’intégration et de formation pour les équipes de ventes.
Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.
Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.
Administrer le programme d’incitatifs de ventes, incluant la publication constante de la performance par rapport aux objectifs.
